summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Photosynthesis is an anabolic, endergonic redox process (ΔG°' = +2870 kJ/mol). Oxygen released originates EXCLUSIVELY from water, not CO2.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Photosynthesis is the physico-chemical process by which photoautotrophic organisms harness solar radiation to synthesize carbohydrates from inorganic carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) and water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$):
$$\Large \mathbf{6\text{CO}_2 + 12\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow[\text{Chloroplast Pigments}]{\text{Light Energy}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 + 6\text{O}_2\uparrow + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \quad (\Delta G^{\circ \prime} = +2870\text{ kJ/mol})}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.1 Historical Experimental Milestones
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.1 Historical Experimental Milestones
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HISTORICAL EXPERIMENTAL MILESTONES
                                         │
  Joseph Priestley (1770)  ──► Candle/Bell Jar/Mint experiment; proved plants restore $\text{O}_2$.
  Jan Ingenhousz (1779)    ──► Showed sunlight & green plant parts are required for $\text{O}_2$ release.
  Julius von Sachs (1854)  ──► Proved glucose is produced & stored as starch inside chloroplasts.
  T. W. Engelmann (1883)   ──► Action Spectrum experiment (*Cladophora* + aerobic bacteria); blue/red light.
  C. van Niel (1931)       ──► Proved $\text{O}_2$ comes from $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (using purple/green sulfur bacteria $\text{H}_2\text{S}$).
  Melvin Calvin (1954)     ──► Traced $C_3$ cycle using $^{14}\text{C}$ in *Chlorella*; identified 3-PGA.
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Joseph Priestley (1770)**: Discovered that a candle burning in a closed bell jar extinguishes and a mouse suffocates. Introducing a mint plant (*Mentha*) restored the 'damaged air' (discovered oxygen in 1774).
2. **Jan Ingenhousz (1779)**: Showed that sunlight is essential; aquatic plants (*Hydrilla*) form oxygen bubbles around green parts only under illumination.
3. **Julius von Sachs (1854)**: Demonstrated that green plant parts synthesize glucose, stored as starch within specialized cellular bodies (chloroplasts).
4. **T.W. Engelmann (1883)**: Split white light using a prism to illuminate green alga *Cladophora* suspended with aerobic bacteria (*Pseudomonas*). Bacteria clustered primarily in the **blue ($430\text{--}470\text{ nm}$)** and **red ($650\text{--}680\text{ nm}$)** regions, generating the **first Action Spectrum**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 Van Niel's Generalized Equation
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Van Niel's Generalized Equation
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
VAN NIEL'S GENERALIZED EQUATION
                        
      2\text{H}_2\text{A} + \text{CO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Light}} 2\text{A} + [\text{CH}_2\text{O}] + \text{H}_2\text{O}
      
   ├── In Green Plants: $\text{H}_2\text{A} = \text{H}_2\text{O} \implies \text{A} = \text{O}_2$ (Oxygenic Photosynthesis)
   └── In Sulfur Bacteria: $\text{H}_2\text{A} = \text{H}_2\text{S} \implies \text{A} = 2\text{S}$ (Anoxygenic Photosynthesis)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Cornelis van Niel demonstrated that photosynthesis is a light-dependent redox reaction where hydrogen from an oxidizable donor ($\text{H}_2\text{A}$) reduces $\text{CO}_2$ to carbohydrate.
• When purple and green sulfur bacteria utilize $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ as hydrogen donor, the byproduct is elemental sulfur ($\text{S}$), **NOT $\text{O}_2$** (Anoxygenic Photosynthesis).
• Hence, van Niel inferred that in green plants, **$\text{O}_2$ is evolved exclusively by the photolysis of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$**, later confirmed with isotopic $^{18}\text{O}$ by Ruben and Kamen (1941).
